name: deutsche-bank-kreditkarte
_note: Deutsche Bank credit card export, verified against real statements 2025-01..2025-12. Five preamble lines (title, card metadata, Abrechnungsdatum) precede the header; parse() finds the header by signature. Two columns are named 'Betrag': index 4 is the FOREIGN amount, index 6 the EUR amount already converted by the bank. Both are addressed by position, never by name — by name the duplicate resolution decides whether a BRL amount gets booked as euros. We take the bank's EUR figure (index 6) so ingested totals reconcile against the printed statement; the card's own FX spread is baked in, which no ECB rate can reproduce. Consequence: the original foreign amount is not retained for these rows. Dates are d.m.Y without zero padding (1.2.2025). balance_row exists so the trailing 'Saldo:' line is consumed rather than counted as an unparseable row — without it a month with no spending (only Saldo 0) trips the all-rows-invalid guard. It captures no anchor: that row carries no date, and the statement date sits on a separate 'Abrechnungsdatum:' preamble line the row parser never sees.
